samples.question: The picture shows a network of grey pipes of equal thickness on white paper. Pipes join only inside the round hubs where they end, and pipes that merely pass near each other are not joined. Three hubs are painted red, green and blue; every hub can be reached from every other hub by travelling along pipe, so all three coloured hubs are connected. Two hubs are said to lie on a common loop when you can travel from one to the other and back again along pipe without using any piece of pipe twice. Exactly one pair of the coloured hubs lies on a common loop. Which two coloured hubs lie on a common loop? Answer 'red and green', 'red and blue', or 'green and blue'.
